absent: Locking, ordering and concurrency rules for table updates, tag storage, notifier registration and cross-CPU table surgery beyond the flag handshake shown.
Semantics, error codes and side effects of host memory-state calls, direct-map eligibility, validity updater, alias flush, and low-level table accessors.
Register-field layouts and permission-bit encodings beyond the abstract per-key shift and mask behavior.
Calling contexts, power-state machine, and restoration guarantees for suspend and resume beyond register transfer shown.
Full table-walk macro expansions, temporary-table setup, and shared-flag storage and visibility guarantees.
Section-size constant value and memory-range enumeration guarantees.

findings.text: Protection-change interface offers batch start and commit operations plus single-entry wrappers that delegate with a count of one.

Start clears the indicated entries and, only on affected hardware when the old entry was user accessible and executable, flushes the address range before returning the old value; commit installs the supplied new entries.
User protection-key access setter exists; it reports lack of hardware support and rejects out-of-range keys before updating hardware state.

Key permission is derived from a fully permissive base by removing write, access, read and execute abilities according to disable requests, then merged into the preserved register value at the key-specific position.
Memory-tagging swap helpers save tags for tagged pages into allocated storage indexed by swap value, and restore tags into pages that accept tagging.

Folio swap preparation saves every constituent page in order and, on failure, invalidates the already-saved prefix before reporting the error; restore walks pages in order with an incrementing swap value.
Tag swap preparation and restore are no-ops without hardware support; save is also a no-op for untagged pages and propagates allocation or table-insert failures after releasing storage.
Page-attribute change carrier holds paired set and clear protection masks; updates always clear first then set so aliased bits resolve deterministically.
Page-attribute walker dispatch binds separate handlers for upper, middle and leaf table levels; upper handlers act only on leaf entries and validate the covered span.
Vmalloc permission changers expose read-only, read-write, no-execute and executable transitions through one common range updater.

Common changer normalizes misalignment with a warning, rejects empty or non-vmalloc ranges, requires coverage by exactly one allocation without huge mapping permission, and flushes lazily unmapped aliases before updating.
Splitting live kernel section mappings can cause translation conflicts, so permission changes are restricted to page-granular vmalloc mappings where splitting is never needed.
When full read-only data protection is enabled, transitions touching the read-only bit are additionally applied page by page to the linear aliases backing the virtual area.
Direct-map controls can mark a page invalid or restore its default valid writable state, set validity over a range, and toggle kernel mapping of pages.
Direct-map and kernel-mapping helpers do nothing or report success without action when the platform forbids direct-map changes.

Realm protection transition is a no-op outside realm world and rejects non-linear addresses; otherwise it breaks the mapping to invalid, requests protected or shared state from the host, then restores validity.
Realm encrypt or decrypt failure warns that the affected pages will be leaked, leaving the caller no safe recovery except leaking.
Realm memory-crypto operations table binds distinct encrypt and decrypt entry points for the realm world.
Kernel page presence probe walks the kernel tables for the linear address of a page and reports whether a valid mapping exists.
Presence probe returns false on any empty intermediate level; for leaf upper levels it returns leaf validity, otherwise it returns final entry validity.
Top-level directory management offers allocation, release and early cache initialization, selecting between direct page handling and slab cache use.
Page-sized top directories bypass the cache; otherwise init creates a naturally aligned cache and enforces extra alignment when very large physical addressing is configured.
Address translation helpers convert linear virtual addresses to physical and kernel symbol addresses to physical with debug checking.
Linear translation warns when given a non-linear address after tag removal; symbol translation asserts the address lies within the kernel image bounds.
Boot initialization validates boot-memory online state and, when hot-remove support is enabled, registers a memory notifier while reporting registration failure.

Boot-memory validation runs only under the debug-memory option; it scans reported memory ranges per section, warns when a section was not marked early, and logs offline boot ranges that could be removed.

Suspend and resume share a context buffer layout with paired register slots at successive small offsets, a platform register slot, and an optional translation-control extension slot when that hardware feature exists.

Low-level suspend saves thread, exception, control and debug-related registers plus cpu offset, stack and platform register; resume restores them while preserving address-size configuration, restoring lock state, access controls and keys.

Non-global kernel mapping installation parks secondaries on reserved tables, lets the boot processor switch tables and rewrite the main kernel tables, then all processors restore the original translation base once a shared completion flag clears.
Cross-processor table surgery relies on a shared flag handshake: secondaries atomically announce readiness and spin until the boot processor finishes, avoiding use of tables under modification.
Full read-only data protection defaults to enabled and is fixed after early initialization.
